prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: After reading the full first round I keep Pd-catalysed C-N coupling as a stand-alone two-laureate prize. It is the only shortlisted candidacy where none of the three criteria the committee has been arguing about is in doubt: attribution is clean (Buchwald and Hartwig, independently, with Kosugi a stoichiometric tin precursor), maturity is not a question after about thirty years of independent confirmation, industrial scale and mechanistic understanding, and no earlier prize covered it. The achievement is a catalytic, ligand-controlled method whose key problem, C-N reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes in competition with beta-hydride elimination, was solved through ligand design and mechanistic work and not by extrapolating the C-C coupling cycle. The round-1 files show no majority forming for B028 or B061 and disagreement on names inside both, so a prize that can be stated in one sentence with two uncontested names is a serious route to five votes, not a fallback.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize is the main objection: some colleagues (Linke, Aqvist, Aili, Chabes) read C-N coupling as an extension of Pd cross-coupling, and Linke finds its generative potential smaller than that of the chemical-biology candidates. I regard the first point as answerable by a citation that names C-N coupling specifically, and the second as a criterion we should not apply to enabling methods, since the impact of this reaction on medicinal and process chemistry is already measured, not hoped for. A real residual weakness is that B008 has had few explicit supporters (Somfai and me), and the one-sentence story is less novel to a broad audience than degradation or base editing.

responses.point: Linke proposes base editing (Liu alone) with PROTACs (Crews and Deshaies) as a two-part prize, and offers B008 as a first alternative, supporting it as a second part beside B061 because two names plus Liu fit within three.
responses.response: I appreciate the offer, but I would not pair B008 with a Liu-only B061. I raised the attribution problem in round 1 and it has not been resolved: your own case against concedes that Komor and Gaudelli were the lead experimentalists and that Kondo and Nishida made a parallel invention, so a Liu-only citation will be challenged, and Chabes wants the opposite. Putting a clean prize beside an open attribution question lowers the quality of the whole configuration. On your direct question, I do accept B008 as a stand-alone prize; and generative potential is a fair criterion, but I read it as the breadth of chemistry a method opens, which for C-N coupling is every amine-containing drug, material and ligand class.

responses.point: Somfai proposes B008 for Buchwald and Hartwig paired with a Liu-only base-editing part, and says B008 should stand alone as a two-laureate prize if B061 does not satisfy the committee on attribution or timing.
responses.response: We agree on B008 and on Kosugi, and the chair's question is aimed at us, so I will answer it: yes, I would carry B008 stand-alone. I would also ask you to reconsider the pairing. Your own case against states that a Liu-only part leaves out Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida, and Chabes and Linke disagree on the names. If B061 cannot be settled, your own words say B008 should stand alone, and I think the committee should decide that now, not at the ballot. Our citations differ only in 'through ligand design'; I am content to adopt your wording provided it keeps C-N coupling named explicitly.

responses.point: Aqvist moved from Car-Parrinello (B037) to B028 as his first choice, because all eight members ranked it and five put it in their top three, while conceding that clinical validation is still accumulating and that the credited list of eight names exceeds the three-name limit.
responses.response: I understand moving toward the candidate with the widest opening support, but breadth of ranking is not the same as readiness for a prize, and your own case against concedes that no degrader is approved and that the cereblon glue strand cannot fit in three names. If, as you write, the Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli trio is not defensible once the glue mechanism is judged inseparable, you are preferring a configuration that you yourself say may have to be abandoned. I find the structural evidence for ternary complexes (VHL and cereblon crystal structures) convincing and I rank B028 as my first alternative for that reason, but I would not vote for it before the committee decides how the glue strand is treated.

responses.point: Chabes proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli for base editing, arguing that the cytosine editor and the adenine editor (evolving TadA to act on DNA) are separate chemical achievements, and accepts that Kondo and Nishida leave a real attribution gap.
responses.response: Your reply about TadA is the first concrete answer to my round-1 question: evolving an RNA-acting adenosine deaminase to work on DNA is a new chemical step, not just a deaminase fusion, and I withdraw the suggestion that the novelty is only the known chemistry. That narrows my objection to attribution and timing, not to the science. But your own account then needs three names for two editor classes plus an unresolved parallel invention by Kondo and Nishida, and the 2020 prize is nearby. A configuration with an acknowledged gap in the credit is harder to defend than one without it, so B061 stays an alternative for me and I do not move it into my configuration.

responses.point: Brzezinski supports B028 for Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, arguing that the field of induced-proximity pharmacology is the right unit, but concedes that the cereblon glue discovery explained an existing drug and may be the more decisive insight and that approved PROTAC drugs are few.
responses.response: I agree with your self-criticism more than with your configuration. If the glue mechanism was the more decisive insight, a PROTAC-only citation recognises the less decisive half of the field. As a colleague at Stockholm University I want it on record that this does not affect my judgement either way. On the chair's question about a criterion between Ciulli and Handa: I would use structural and mechanistic evidence for the central claim, and for the glue strand that is the cereblon-thalidomide binding and degron work, which is real, but it does not resolve the three-name limit. That makes B028 harder to credit cleanly than B008, whose two names are not contested.

uncertainties: Whether a majority accepts C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 prize when the citation names C-N coupling explicitly; I cannot know that without the vote.

Whether the committee will resolve the B028 attribution (Ciulli or Handa, PROTACs or glues) and the B061 attribution (Liu alone or three names, Kondo and Nishida) well enough for either to reach five votes; if so my judgement of the relative maturity would be less decisive than I now think.
Whether I give too little weight to degradation because of my own distance from chemical biology; I defer to colleagues on the biological evidence, but I am confident about the structural evidence.
statement.conflict_note: No change. I have no collaboration or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or any other shortlisted candidate. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Secretary Peter Brzezinski, which does not bear on any candidacy in my configuration. My field is electron crystallography and porous materials, so I am less equipped to judge the chemical biology candidates and defer to colleagues on the biological evidence.
